items.subtype_name: Find the margin of error from a given interval
items.stimulus: A highway agency tested 64 randomly selected concrete cylinders cast during a single bridge-deck pour. The mean compressive strength of the sampled cylinders was 42 megapascals (MPa). Based on the sample, it is estimated that the mean compressive strength of all cylinders cast during that pour is between 39 MPa and 45 MPa.
items.stem: What is the associated margin of error?
items.explanation: The interval is the sample mean plus or minus the margin of error. Subtract the sample mean from the upper bound: $45 - 42 = 3$. Check the other side: $42 - 39 = 3$. Both sides match, so the margin of error is 3 MPa.

B.why: You found the full width of the interval, $45 - 39 = 6$. The interval runs one margin below the mean and one margin above it, so you need half of that width.

C.why: 39 MPa is the lower end of the interval. The margin of error is how far that end is from the mean, not the end itself.

D.why: 45 MPa is the upper end of the interval. The margin of error is the distance from 42 up to 45, not the endpoint.

A.why: You halved the margin of error a second time. Either you found $0.75$ and divided by 2 again, or you divided the full width of $1.50$ by 4. The margin of error is the full distance from \$18.40 to an endpoint, which is \$0.75.

C.why: You found the full width of the interval, $19.15 - 17.65 = 1.50$. That width covers one margin below the sample mean and one above, so it's twice the margin of error.

D.why: You gave the interval's upper endpoint. \$19.15 is the top of the plausible range, not the distance between that boundary and the sample mean.
